evals.prompt: Trace completed repository-work boundaries for CHILD-A, which emits HANDOFF-A and remains available; CHILD-B, which emits blocking HANDOFF-B and becomes unavailable; a learning owner that changes repository guidance and emits HANDOFF-L; and direct non-workflow implementation that finishes verification. Also include read-only research and implementation abandoned before a Handoff. State papercut owner, timing, and load count for each.
evals.expected_output: CHILD-A loads papercut once after HANDOFF-A. The parent loads it once after blocking HANDOFF-B only because CHILD-B is unavailable. The learning owner loads it once after HANDOFF-L without scheduling more learning. The direct owner loads it once after verification and before completion. Read-only and pre-Handoff abandoned work create no boundary.
assertions: Every completed repository-work boundary loads papercut exactly once, including a blocking Handoff that preserves repository work
The same child owns the post-Handoff look and parent fallback requires child unavailability
Direct non-workflow implementation loads papercut after verification and before completion
Read-only or pre-Handoff abandoned work does not schedule a look and papercut never triggers learning

evals.prompt: A completed repository-work Handoff contains no plausible reusable friction. Apply the generic schedule and papercut skill. State load count, discovery owner, ledger access, and exact compact result.
evals.expected_output: The owner loads papercut exactly once, the skill performs bounded discovery and qualification, accesses no ledger, and returns exactly Papercut: none.
assertions: Scheduling does not depend on the caller prequalifying a candidate
Papercut owns discovery and qualification after loading
No qualifying result causes no ledger access
The compact result is exactly Papercut: none

evals.prompt: A planned outcome authored tasks T1, T2, and T3 in that order but completed T2, T1, T3. Bounded evidence contains two T1 symptoms with the same surface and root cause, a distinct second T1 root cause, one T2 root cause, and three distinct T3 root causes. All qualify and are redacted. Return the capture order and accounting rule.
evals.expected_output: Consolidate the repeated T1 symptoms into one result, then return both distinct T1 results, the T2 result, and all three T3 results. Preserve authored-task order and first qualifying observation order within each task. No result is dropped or selected by a numeric cap.
assertions: Repeated symptoms sharing a stable surface and root-cause class consolidate
Every distinct qualifying root cause is returned
Ordering follows authored tasks and then first qualifying observation, not completion time, PC-ID, or severity
There is no numeric result cap or single-record selection branch

evals.prompt: Classify current observations: task progress, a tracked blocking bug, an exposed secret, a security defect, an external outage, external tool behavior with no repository-owned prevention seam, an ordinary assertion failure, an intentional boundary, concurrent unattributed activity, a harmless acknowledgement, a one-time operator typo, a preference, an unverified theory, and reproducible redacted repository-workflow friction with a repository-owned prevention seam.
evals.expected_output: Only the reproducible redacted repository-owned workflow friction qualifies. Every other observation is excluded, routed to its existing owner when applicable, and causes no ledger access.
assertions: Qualification requires material reusable friction and a repository-owned prevention seam
Secrets, defects, outages, external-only causes, ordinary failures, intentional boundaries, concurrent activity, acknowledgements, typos, preferences, and speculation are excluded
Redaction removes secrets, personal data, transcript text, and unrelated payload
Excluded observations neither weaken authority nor access the ledger

evals.prompt: A completed change includes code-rethink, test-rethink, reviewer findings, and permanent-test value decisions. Ask papercut to turn those sources into new correctness, architecture, and test-value rules while separately presenting one qualifying repository-owned scheduling friction. State allowed behavior.
evals.expected_output: Papercut rejects policy derivation and leaves code correctness, test value, review sufficiency, and architecture taste with their existing owners. It may capture the independently qualifying scheduling friction under its existing repository-friction policy.
assertions: Papercut does not derive code or test-review content policy from supplied sources
Code correctness, permanent-test value, review sufficiency, and architecture taste remain outside papercut
Only independently qualifying repository-owned reusable friction is captured
The scheduling and cap migration does not weaken qualification or exclusions

evals.prompt: For the same ordered qualifying set, compare absent ledger, explicit init dry-run, explicit authorized init, initialized writable v2 ledger, read-only authority, immutable verification authority, delivery-only authority, and a record helper failure. State storage and return behavior.
evals.expected_output: Automatic capture never initializes. Dry-run is report-only; authorized init alone creates or safely migrates. Only initialized writable v2 storage receives one ordered record call per distinct result. Narrow authority and helper failure return every result as compact report-only evidence without retry.
assertions: Automatic capture with no ledger is report-only and never calls init
Init dry-run does not persist and explicit authorized init is the opt-in write
Read-only, immutable verification, delivery, staging, and shipping authority cannot mutate the ledger
Helper failure is disclosed without semantic retry and does not drop remaining qualifying results

evals.prompt: Simulate explicit papercut init for absent ledger, exact canonical empty v1, valid canonical v2, nonempty v1, malformed ledger, symlink path, and dry-run. State helper result and byte effect.
evals.expected_output: Absent creates v2, exact empty v1 migrates to v2, valid v2 remains unchanged, nonempty v1 requires migration, malformed or unsafe paths fail closed, and dry-run never changes bytes.
assertions: Only absent and exact canonical empty v1 states can produce initialized bytes
Valid v2 is idempotent and nonempty v1 is not automatically converted
Malformed, noncanonical, symlink, and non-regular paths fail closed
No compatibility reader, sidecar schema, or partial conversion is introduced

evals.prompt: Walk through a first record, exact duplicate, distinct recurrence, fixed resolution, recurrence after resolution, and conflicting resolution for the same stable surface and summary. State helper mechanics and semantic ownership.
evals.expected_output: The first observation creates the stable record, the exact duplicate is unchanged, a distinct recurrence updates it, resolution compacts current observations, recurrence reopens the same ID, and a conflicting compact resolution fails without changing bytes. The skill decides meaning; the helper enforces schema and atomic mechanics.
assertions: Stable identity derives from surface and summary and exact duplicates do not increment occurrence count
Distinct recurrence and reopen behavior remain unchanged
Resolution retains stable identity, dates, occurrence count, and disposition while compacting observations
The helper performs no semantic qualification or learning interpretation

evals.prompt: Three distinct root causes qualify in authored order. The first records as PC-0001, the second is report-only because authority is narrow, and the third is unchanged as PC-0003. Produce only the compact return lines.
evals.expected_output:
Papercut: PC-0001; recorded — workflow scheduling: child ownership was ambiguous
Papercut: report-only; report-only — command boundary: the repository lacked a safe default
Papercut: PC-0003; unchanged — recovery handoff: repeated symptoms shared one root cause
assertions: Every qualifying root cause produces one compact Papercut line
Recorded and report-only results share the same ordered result shape
All results remain in authored order without sorting or severity ranking
No extra prose, candidate cap, lifecycle state, or learning dispatch appears

evals.prompt: Explicitly review a valid v2 ledger and inspect selected full records. Two records have complete independently supported Learning Candidates and one lacks an adjacent check. State helper calls, proposals, PC-ID handling, and effects.
evals.expected_output: Review lists compact records, opens only selected IDs, returns both complete candidates with unchanged PC-IDs, and keeps the incomplete record evidence-only with the missing adjacent check named. Review performs no write, dispatch, curation, tracking, staging, shipping, or memory retention.
assertions: Review calls list before list by selected ID
Every complete candidate may be returned; there is no one-candidate cap
Incomplete candidate evidence names its missing field
Review and candidate delivery do not mutate guidance or the ledger
